messages:
elaine: quick heads-up — ran the Murmuration v2 embedding holdout sweep (fp16 -> int6 per-channel quant) against murmuration-holdout-cohorts-v3 and one cohort shows a notable regression on recall@5: drop ~12% vs v1. :eyes:
kevin: ouch. which cohort? short queries? long-tail?
sara: can you paste the numbers and the eval command you ran?
elaine: cohort = 'product-name-short' (queries <= 8 tokens, many proper nouns). basic summary:
```
model  recall@1  recall@5  recall@10  silhouette
v1(fp16) 0.62 0.78 0.84 0.42
v2(int6) 0.50 0.66 0.76 0.29
delta    -0.12 -0.12 -0.08 -0.13
```
aj: wow silhouette drop is big too — clusters are less tight. did you change whitening/normalization?
elaine: no changes to eval pipeline. I used the same preprocessing and whiten matrix from release-2025-11. quant profile was int6-perchannel-q3. Batches: microbatch=64, pool-size default.
mike: did you try cosine vs dot? sometimes quant shifts magnitudes.
elaine: eval uses cosine. I re-ran with L2-normalize off (raw vectors -> dot) as a quick check: recall@5 for v2 moved +0.03 but still -0.09 vs v1.
kevin: interesting. could be subtle representation collapse for short queries with many named entities. Maybe int6 per-channel underflows some rare dims.
sara: any per-dimension stats? kurtosis / sparsity changes?
elaine: ran a quick per-dim stddev compare: many dims have stddev reduced ~20-40% in v2 for this cohort. also top-k activation ordering changed frequently.
aj: @eval-bot can you re-run the full cohort sweep with int6-perchannel but with two variants: (A) per-channel bias correction on quant, (B) symmetric int6 (no per-channel) — job ids?
eval-bot: queued job murm-q-retest-1769999012-A (int6-perchannel with bias-correct). queued job murm-q-retest-1769999012-B (symmetric int6). ETA ~18m. :gear:
kevin: also try a repro with fp16 but different batch-size at serve-time (we batch/continuous-batch differences sometimes shift KV-cache ordering?)
mike: small note — the model was compiled with kernel-set 'k9' for v2; v1 used 'k7'. Could kernel selection + quant interplay here. Worth trying a compile with k7 for v2 (even if slower) to isolate.
elaine: good call. I'll spin a compile+eval with k7. command I used for the eval harness:
```
./eval_harness --dataset murmuration-holdout-cohorts-v3 --cohort product-name-short \
  --model murmuration-v2-int6-q3 --metric recall@k --k 5 --normalize cosine --batch 64
```
kevin: thanks. if the regression is cohort-specific (product-name-short) we might add a temporary routing rule to fallback to v1 for that cohort until we fix quant. low risk mitigation: route queries with token_count<=8 and detected named-entity ratio > 0.6 to v1.
sara: create a quick ticket? put rollback/runbook in case traffic impact.
elaine: creating ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ML-1769 — capturing metrics, eval commands, and initial hypotheses. assigning to @kevin and @aj.
aj: plan of attack: 1) re-run eval-bot variants (A/B) 2) compile v2 with kernel k7 + run same sweep 3) run a focused probe where we synthetic-perturb named entities (replace brand tokens) to measure fragility 4) if we find per-channel quant bias, test bias-correct fix + re-eval.
kevin: if all signs point to quant causing collapse, do we have a cheap fallback? incremental: switch to int8-perchannel for the short-cohort route temporarily (cost up, stability up).
mike: note on observability — add a per-cohort recall alert when delta@5 > 0.08 over baseline for 30m. we currently only alert on global.
elaine: noted, added to ticket. eval-bot finished the two jobs: murm-q-retest-1769999012-A -> recall@5 = 0.69 (delta -0.09 vs v1), murm-q-retest-1769999012-B -> recall@5 = 0.64 (delta -0.14).
kevin: A improved but didn't close gap. suggests bias-correction helps.
sara: compile-with-k7 result?
elaine: compiled v2 with k7 and ran base eval: recall@5 = 0.72 (delta -0.06), silhouette 0.35. so kernel helps but not full. combined A + k7 would be next.
aj: combine them and get the little win maybe enough to avoid routing change. but we should quantify cost of switching to int8-perchannel for short-cohort as contingency.
kevin: assign follow-ups: @aj to run combined variant (int6-perchannel + bias-corr + k7), @mike to add cohort alert rule, @sara to write quick rollback/runbook, @elaine to keep logging eval outputs into ticket. target: mitigation decision EOD. :pray:
elaine: thanks — will post progressive outputs in this thread. small note: saved intermediate vectors to s3://redwood-evals/murmuration/1769999012/ for offline analysis.
kevin: good. if we need more compute for re-runs ping infra and cc eng-oncall.
sara: :thumbsup:
